ocean-acidification-carbonate.alt: Carbon dioxide from the air dissolves in the surface ocean. CO2 + H2O forms H2CO3, carbonic acid, which releases a hydrogen ion and a bicarbonate ion (H+ + HCO3-): more hydrogen ions, so pH falls. Hydrogen ions also combine with carbonate ions (H+ + CO3 2- gives HCO3-), so fewer carbonate ions are left for corals and shellfish to build calcium carbonate. A pH scale below shows average surface ocean pH of about 8.2 around 1750, about 8.1 today and about 7.8 by 2100 if emissions stay high.
